# Implementation Plan: Dedicated Contact Page & Sanity CMS Scaffold

**Branch**: `002-build-dedicated-contact` | **Date**: 2025-10-31 | **Spec**: `/specs/002-build-dedicated-contact/spec.md`  
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-build-dedicated-contact/spec.md`

**Note**: This template is generated by `/speckit.plan`. Every decision recorded here MUST reference the Nyan Cat Space constitution and demonstrate compliance before implementation begins.

## Summary

Ship a first-class contact experience and future-proof blog foundation without breaking the cosmic terminal vibe. The new `contact.html` becomes the primary conversion surface: a Netlify-backed form with inline `aria-live` success banner, keyboard-friendly controls, spam guard, and resilient fallbacks when JavaScript or motion is disabled. In parallel, scaffold a Sanity.io-powered blog informed by “Using Sanity.io with Vanilla JavaScript for a Static Portfolio Site.pdf”: define datasets, environment variables, and a lightweight client helper so published posts can render on a new `blog.html` while the empty state stays on-brand. Target users include collaborators reaching out via email and readers exploring upcoming blog content; both flows must respect constitution gates for accessibility, performance, and narrative clarity.

## Technical Context

**Languages**: HTML5, Tailwind CSS utilities, vanilla JavaScript (ES2020)  
**Dependencies**: `styles/tailwind.css` (hand-authored utility set); no build tooling, frameworks, or external JS libraries; Netlify Forms attributes handled in markup; Sanity Content Lake queried via native `fetch` with GROQ derived from the PDF reference  
**Assets**: Media stored under `assets/`; individual files ≤ 200KB unless a variance is justified in Constitution Check  
**Validation**: Manual accessibility sweeps (keyboard navigation, contrast, reduced motion), responsive testing across mobile/desktop, Netlify form submission test, Sanity mock data verification, optional automated linting if available  
**Target Platforms**: Evergreen desktop/mobile browsers, graceful fallback with JavaScript disabled  
**Performance Goals**: First meaningful paint < 2s on LTE, animation frame budgets ≤ 16ms, zero blocking network requests after initial page load; Sanity fetch runs post-load and caches results in-memory  
**Constraints**: Preserve retro terminal aesthetic, respect prefers-reduced-motion, stay fully static (no build tooling), maintain accessible content hierarchy, inline success banner only (no redirect)  
**Scope**: Existing static pages plus new `contact.html` and `blog.html`, shared assets, Sanity helper, environment documentation

## Constitution Check

*Gate: MUST pass before Phase 0 research. Re-validate after Phase 1 design.*

- **Terminal Fidelity**: Contact and blog pages reuse the black background + neon palette, monospace typography, and console blocks. Tailwind utilities may gain a scoped form layout class (`form-grid-terminal`) while respecting the command-line aesthetic. Navigation items use same hover/focus glow as existing pages. Inline success banner mimics a terminal output line with green text.  
- **Cosmic Performance & Simplicity**: No new build step; Netlify form relies on HTML attributes, and Sanity integration uses a single helper under 2 KB (GZIP) loaded only on `blog.html`. Fetch executes after `DOMContentLoaded` to avoid blocking first paint. Form validation leans on native constraints with light JS enhancements to respect the <10 KB JS budget.  
- **Universal Accessibility**: `contact.html` keeps the skip link target, landmark roles (`main`, `form`), and explicit labels. Error/success feedback uses `aria-live` and `aria-invalid`. Blog empty state and post list maintain heading hierarchy (`h1` page title, `h2` per post). Reduced-motion preference disables any animated success or scroll cues, and the inline banner fades without transitions when `prefers-reduced-motion` is set.  
- **Playful Animation Discipline**: Only subtle pulses on focus/hover; no new auto-running animations beyond optional gradient shimmer, which will be disabled under reduced motion. Contact success banner appears with CSS transition gated by motion media query. Blog page avoids marquee effects; any highlight uses static styling.  
- **Narrative & Content Clarity**: Navigation updated to point to `contact.html` and `blog.html`, keeping story beats coherent (Home, About, Projects, Contact, Blog). Contact intro copy references sending “space mail,” and blog header frames posts as “captain’s log entries,” aligning with cosmic narrative while clarifying state (published posts vs. empty). Footer and skip link remain intact to preserve flow across breakpoints.
